what_is_measured: capacitance measured directly (transient or membrane test; tau/Rin is a proxy), tau, access resistance and bridge balance by genotype; the stated cell-selection rule (the Wwox identity check uses Rin and tau, which are compared variables); the measured junction potential of the actual solutions; age, weight, layer, area, temperature; recording with and without synaptic blockers
controls_from_the_first_slice: littermate WT, HT, KO in the same slice batches; identity by morphology or marker
decides: E3 (size or maturation) and E4 (recording) against E2; whether the borrowed -13 mV is the right size

what_is_measured: Rin, rest, sag, rebound with synaptic transmission intact versus blocked, in bursting and non-bursting KO and HT slices
controls_from_the_first_slice: same cells before and after blockers; vehicle time control
controls_that_can_follow: extracellular K+ read in bursting slices

what_is_measured: current-clamp Rin share and voltage-clamp difference current of a low-micromolar Ba2+ (the producer's source used 60 uM) over about -130 to -60 mV, with TTX and synaptic blockers, zero-crossing against E_K computed for the measured junction potential, per pF
controls_from_the_first_slice: WT and HT in the same batches; vehicle; a second Ba2+ concentration to see the leak component (the 200 uM source shows more)
controls_that_can_follow: a Kir2 blocker named in the literature (not read here)
decides: KH1: is the Ba2+-sensitive current smaller per pF, and does the Rin and rest pair follow the implied reversal

what_is_measured: the same difference-current and Rin read with a higher Ba2+ concentration (the 200 uM source blocks a further leak component) and with a K2P blocker group read in the literature (A1899 and fluoxetine in 40595546, adult dendritic), at the concentrations of the sources
controls_from_the_first_slice: vehicle; WT and HT; engagement shown first
decides: whether the Ba2+-resistant or K2P-type leak differs, so that outcome O2 can close the K branch only for the families tested

arm: Kv7 difference current at a depolarised holding potential
what_is_measured: XE991-sensitive current at about -55 to -45 mV (not at rest: D05), mAHP and adaptation in current clamp, a second blocker chemotype (linopirdine)
controls_from_the_first_slice: WT and HT; vehicle; XE991 in WT as the genotype-independent baseline
controls_that_can_follow: retigabine at matched effect size (see step 6)
decides: KH2: a spiking-range Kv7 deficit; F-I slope at matched rheobase

what_is_measured: ZD7288-sensitive current per pF and matched-deflection sag with a second chemotype
controls_that_can_follow: ivabradine as a second chemotype only after engagement is shown
decides: KH3: the share of sag and rebound that is Ih

what_is_measured: add a leak of about 2.7 nS with reversal at E_K (set on the recorded scale with the measured junction potential) to KO and HT neurons, and subtract it in WT, then re-read Rin, rest, sag, rebound, rheobase and gain; compare the restored tau with the WT tau (18.5 ms if C is the WT value, 15.3 ms if C is the KO value; C measured directly)
controls_from_the_first_slice: a sham conductance of zero; a leak of the same size with reversal at the WT rest (it moves Rin without moving rest); a leak at 0 mV (a seal-like shunt) to separate a K+ reversal from a depolarising shunt
decides: sufficiency only: any hyperpolarising conductance restores Rin and rest in a smaller or leaky cell, so restoration does not separate E2 from E3/E4; the per-pF currents of steps 0 and 2 do. If restoration also restores sag and rebound, recruitment explains them
state: conditional on step 2 giving a smaller Ba2+-sensitive current per pF

what_is_measured: a Kv7 opener only if step 3 shows a spiking-range deficit; matched input-output reduction control (the AMPA/kainate pair of IT41 on the evoked-charge axis; a sodium-channel-blocking antiseizure class as a mechanism-different comparator at a matched fall of evoked firing)
controls_from_the_first_slice: vehicle; the effect on WT cells at the same concentration
decides: mechanism effect versus general suppression versus a worse function (AHP, sag, resting state)
